[element-date-in-citation]
=== `<date-in-citation>` Date in Citation (in a citation)

A container element for any date that may be referenced in a citation, other than the publication date of the cited work. The <<attribute-content-type,`@content-type`>> attribute should be used to identify the purpose/type of date.

#### Usage/Remarks
For example, if the `<date-in-citation>` element contains the date on which a contributor examined the cited work, the attribute might be “`access-date`”. Some online resources are changing so quickly that a citation to the resource is not complete without the date on which the cited resource was examined, since a day before or a day later the relevant material might be different. This element can be used to record such an access date.

Any combination of: Text, numbers, or special characters <<element-day,`<day>`>> <<element-day,Day (in a citation)>> <<element-era,`<era>`>> <<element-era,Era (in a citation)>> <<element-month,`<month>`>> <<element-month,Month (in a citation)>> <<element-season,`<season>`>> <<element-season,Season (in a citation)>> <<element-year,`<year>`>> <<element-year,Year>>

</ref>

</ref>
